steps.title: Collect strays, not perfection
steps.text: Early on you have few rooms and little furniture, so breeding is slow. Take every stray out on adventures and keep them unless you run out of space; the game is about numbers at this stage. Strays left outside the house are not fed.

steps.title: Check the kittens every morning
steps.text: Look over the night's kittens. Poor stats, a bad mutation or a disorder that will hurt: send them to Tink. Ten kittens unlock the first details on your cats, and his first two upgrades show base stats and inbreeding.

steps.title: Feed Butch first
steps.text: Send him cats that have been to the Sewers or Junkyard. Storage is the first real bottleneck, because the Boneyard and Junkyard drop very good items.

steps.title: Then Tracy, Frank and Jack
steps.text: Tracy gives food storage, totems and blank collars. Frank gives rooms. Jack sells furniture. The basic upgrades of these vendors cost about 45 cats in total. Storage upgrades only work once you place them in the house like furniture.

steps.title: Buy stimulation and appeal
steps.text: Furniture with Stimulation improves the stats and abilities that kittens inherit; Appeal brings better strays. Stock refreshes every Sunday, so buy food only in a way that lets you refresh the shop.

steps.title: Read the enemies, take the hard path when sure
steps.text: Right-click an enemy to see its movement and attack range. The hard path adds one fight and so one level-up, but skipping it is fine if your team is not ready.

steps.title: Know who takes which cats
steps.text: Do not wait for an old cat to die: donate it to the right neighbour first. Who takes what:

items.name: Butch
items.text: cats that have adventured (Sewers or Junkyard first).

items.name: Dr. Beanies
items.text: mutated, deformed, diseased or disordered cats, 5 per quest item.

items.name: Mystery Man
items.text: cats that died, on a run or at home.

npcs.name: Butch
npcs.takes: Retired cats that have adventured (Sewers or Junkyard first)
gives: Unlocks a class each time you finish a zone and talk to him
npcs.tip: Use the storage filters before you throw anything away; items thrown in the trash by mistake are gone.

npcs.name: Tracy
gives: Totems (+5 to a random house stat, with special effects)
Blank collars (up to 3, duplicate a random class)
npcs.tip: Upgrades only work once you physically place the storage in the house. The class of each blank collar shows on the box before a run.

npcs.name: Frank
gives: Each room holds 4-5 cats before comfort goes negative
npcs.tip: Until he has 25 cats you are limited to about 8 good cats at a time. Aim for the attic and two rooms.

npcs.name: Baby Jack
npcs.tip: His stock resets every Sunday, so check the calendar in the top left.

npcs.name: Tink
npcs.tip: Take at least the first two upgrades. Without them you cannot see a cat's base stats or whether it is inbred. Do not level him past that.

npcs.name: Dr. Beanies
npcs.takes: Mutated, deformed, diseased or disordered cats (5 per quest item)
gives: Side quest items with a penalty, then a rare or legendary reward
npcs.tip: Last NPC you unlock. Do the house boss quest items first; the side quests can wait.

npcs.name: Mystery Man
npcs.takes: Cats that die on a run or at home
gives: Upgrades for each batch of dead cats
npcs.tip: Early Game Tips calls the NPC who takes dead cats the Organ Grinder; the trophy list calls him Mystery Man. It is probably the same one.

note: Order and numbers come from Greenside's Getting Started guide, Early Game Tips and the Steam 100% achievement guide. Which NPC to level first is an opinion: all three guides put Butch first.
